newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas granted additional Europe capacity.
newsitem.headline: Qantas granted additional Europe capacity.

text.p: The International Air Services Commission said on Thursday it had allocated capacity on the France route to Qantas Airways Ltd which would allow it to start code share services to Paris with British Airways Plc.
Commission chairman Jim Bain said in a statement Qantas would operate its own aircraft as far as London and then codeshare with British Airways' flights between London and Paris.
The arrangement would start from July 5 and Qantas would provide 150 seats a day on the route.
Bain said the commission also had made an interim decision to allocate one Boeing 747 equivalent of capacity to Qantas on the Austria route.
Qantas, which is 25 percent owned by BA, would operate seven flights a week to Vienna, using its own aircraft to London and then code sharing with BA between London and Vienna.

"The commission proposes granting a three-year determination rather than the five years sought by Qantas, to enable the commission to assess the implications of Qantas using all seven available code share frequencies while using only one-third of the available capacity," Bain said.
